summary: Independent review of the RECLAIM1 conditional opportunity reset (the #943 amendment). First pin for this PR; I withheld on cc9b80a for a P1 and re-reviewed from scratch at af31b02. THE AMENDMENT IS CORRECT, verified in code rather than from the description: _flip_owner_confirmation_closed requires expected_rows <= confirmed_rows, so EVERY sibling row must carry a confirmation close keyed on this opportunity's fanout_slot_id, and a partial or failed fan-out therefore CONSUMES; the old unconditional unknown_preflip_owner_flat_after_settle retire (the DBGI hole) is now gated on that proof with the unproven path landing in a new 'consumed' phase; 'consumed' is refused by _strict_first_rest_admitted as owner_phase_consumed, while _end_flip_owner_on_sell falls through to _retire_flip_owner_opportunity(sell_flip_flat) so a genuine SELL flip releases it (TNON's case); and _retire_flip_owner_opportunity clears the segment id and owner memory so the next mint takes a NEW id, i.e. the identity genuinely rotates. Both operator-requested controls are BEHAVIOURAL rather than classification tables — the DBGI stop-close control asserts drain_pending_intents() == [], proving the consumed state actually blocks a re-entry, and the two-successive-false-flips control asserts the second opportunity id is strictly greater than the first. THE P1 I RAISED ON cc9b80a AND ITS FIX: with #945 merged dark, _load_confirmation_entries sets fanout_slot_id='' (schwab_1m_v2_bot.py:1257), that empty value flows into the emitted confirmation payload (schwab_1m_v2.py:5529) and into #947's new stamp confirmation_fanout_slot_id (oms/service.py:5107); the original reader then treated it as malformed and returned FlipPositionBook(readable=False) for the WHOLE book, and apply_flip_position_book sets flip_owner_evidence_readable=False for EVERY symbol. I proved the consequence rather than asserting it: two idle unrelated symbols both admitted True, one unreadable book applied, both then admitted False — a fleet-wide entry stop, and non-transient because the malformed order stays inside the session query window. At af31b02 an empty slot_id is skipped_unbound with a warning and a continue, local to that close; a missing row id/symbol/account is counted malformed and also skipped; four readable=False sites remain for genuine read failures. Skipping is conservative by construction: it shrinks confirmed_rows, so expected_rows <= confirmed_rows fails and the segment stays consumed — a skipped close can never cause a wrong reset. Mutations, all independently RED against test_v2_flip_owned_first_entry.py + test_confirmation_exit_fanout.py + test_v2_flip_entry_ownership_store.py (67 passed baseline): reinstate the fleet-wide poison on an empty slot id -> 1 failed; accept an unbound close as proof -> 1; confirmation always proven -> 6; partial fan-out accepted -> 3; consumed admits entry -> 1; and the DISCRIMINATION check, turning the genuine malformed_open_managed_row fail-closed into a continue -> 1 failed (test_malformed_open_managed_row_still_fails_the_position_book_closed), so the fix did not trade a fleet-wide poison for never failing closed. METHOD CORRECTION RECORDED: my first attempt at that discrimination mutation appeared to SURVIVE because it hit the wrong readable=False site (line 1646, a different function) instead of the managed-row path; retargeted it is red. An incomplete mutation is not a surviving mutant. Controlled full unit pair vs base 784057e1: base 46 failed/3591 passed, head 46 failed/3603 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed, compared as sorted sets. Ruff clean. Ancestor test PASS. ⛔ DEPLOY CONSTRAINT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS PR: even with the P1 fixed, #947 with #945 still dark is strictly more conservative on Webull-only names — no confirmation decision exists for them, so every exit consumes the segment including a genuine false flip, and the operator's multiple-false-flips rule does not work on Schwab-refused symbols until #945 is ENABLED. Enabling #945 requires a strategy-service restart because self.settings is built once and never reloaded, and that restart necessarily also activates this amendment, so the two must ship in the SAME restart step.
